gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's own C2000 Gen 2 page lists the BP2000 (Gen 2) expansion battery as its add-on battery for 'up to 4kWh', an 800 W Alternator Charger rated '100% in 3 Hr', and a 10 ms UPS switchover, alongside a TT-30R rated 120 V / 20 A / 2,400 W max. Together those make it the TT-30 model whose maker documents the most RV pairings, now that BLUETTI's US store marks the AC200L and every AC200L bundle 'Discontinued'.
standout_why: Compared against Dealectric's own current page, theoutagebrief.com's 2kWh shootout, OutdoorGearLab's power station roundup and the bluettipower.com AC200L page ChatGPT cited. The Dealectric page gives the C2000 Gen 2's TT-30R as 20 A but says nothing about expansion batteries for any model and names no alternator charger. theoutagebrief.com has no TT-30, expansion or alternator information except 'Jackery 2000 v2 not expandable'. OutdoorGearLab doesn't cover the C2000 Gen 2 and only notes that the Jackery 2000 v2 can't take an expansion battery. The AC200L's discontinued status is not new, because the bluettipower.com page ChatGPT cited on 2026-11-13 already shows it, and ChatGPT repeated it. Popular Mechanics blocked fetching, so I couldn't check it.
decides: The AC200L is still ChatGPT's top pick in every chat, but BLUETTI's US store now lists the base unit and all its bundles as 'Discontinued'. On 2026-10-31 our page said it was in stock. That makes the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 the TT-30 pick the maker fully documents: a TT-30R at 120 V / 20 A / 2,400 W, one expansion path (BP2000 Gen 2, up to about 4 kWh), an 800 W alternator charger for charging while driving, and a 10 ms UPS. One caveat: Anker's page showed no price today, so the under-$900 condition is still unconfirmed. The Elite 200 V2 at $899 has no RV outlet, and BLUETTI's box list doesn't include an RV adapter, so a TT-30 hookup means buying a separate adapter, which then limits you to that outlet's 20 A.
